correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the covariance using independent uniform ranks. An edge inside a decreasing triple contributes 1/12; a singly shared extreme contributes signed 1/24 because its conditional mean is 3/4 or 1/4, and a shared middle contributes zero. With A=i−1 and B=n−i, triples containing i contribute binom(n−1,2)/6 plus [binom(B,2)(B−A−2)+binom(A,2)(A−B−2)]/24. Other triples contribute 1/12 only when they straddle i, giving AB(n−3)/24. This simplifies to (1); AB≤(n−1)^2/4 gives the positive central lower bound, including n=3, and the claimed positional monotonicity. Conditional on X_i=x, D_i has A Bernoulli(1−x) and B Bernoulli(x) terms, independent conditionally, so total variance is (n−1)/6+(A−B)^2/12. For T, disjoint triples give no covariance and pairs with at least two shared indices are O(n^4). The single-index projection gives the main term. With y=x−1/2, its scaled limit is [(1−2t)y+(1−6t+6t²)(y²−1/12)]/4. The two terms are orthogonal in x, with x-moments 1/12 and 1/180 and squared t-integrals 1/3 and 1/5, giving 13/7200. Uniform O(1/n) projection error and the polynomial Riemann sum give the O(n^4) remainder. The normalized covariance tends to 1/96 on the stated scale, the degree variance divided by n tends to (1+2s²)/6, and outside the window that latter ratio diverges while normalized covariance is bounded. This proves the constant and both regimes.
residual_risks: The supplied finite replay path is python3 verify_degree_triangles.py; the checker is corroborative, not relied on for either universal claim. The priority discussion could more precisely say that the triple indicator can be written as a product of two comparisons by transitivity; either representation still requires more than pairwise second moments for the mixed covariance.
